display: The Forerunner: opening piece, paragraph 1
text: You are your own forerunner, and the towers you have builded are but the foundation of your giant-self. And that self too shall be a foundation.
note: Growth: what we build is foundation for more

tags.when_helps: For someone unsure of their progress who needs to hear their efforts are foundations for a greater self.

display_text: You are your own forerunner, and the towers you have builded are but the foundation of your giant-self. And that self too shall be a foundation.
plain: You go ahead of yourself: everything you have built is only the base for a greater self, and that self in turn will be a base for more.
core_idea: You are always building toward a larger self

display: The Forerunner: opening piece, paragraph 3
text: Always have we been our own forerunners, and always shall we be. And all that we have gathered and shall gather shall be but seeds for fields yet unploughed. We are the fields and the ploughmen, the gatherers and the gathered.
note: Lifelong becoming; we are seed and harvest

tags.when_helps: For someone wondering whether what they gather in life will bear fruit.

display_text: Always have we been our own forerunners, and always shall we be. And all that we have gathered and shall gather shall be but seeds for fields yet unploughed. We are the fields and the ploughmen, the gatherers and the gathered.
plain: We have always gone ahead of ourselves and always will. All we gather is only seed for fields not yet ploughed; we are both the fields and the ploughmen, the harvesters and the harvest.
core_idea: We are both the sowers and the harvest

display: The Forerunner: Love, paragraph 3
text: O love, whose lordly hand Has bridled my desires, And raised my hunger and my thirst To dignity and pride, Let not the strong in me and the constant Eat the bread or drink the wine That tempt my weaker self. Let me rather starve, And let my heart parch with thirst, And let me die and perish, Ere I stretch my hand To a cup you did not fill, Or a bowl you did not bless.
note: Self-restraint in love; refusing lesser temptations

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
keywords: a cup you did not fill
tags.when_helps: For someone resisting temptation who wants their desires governed by love.

display_text: O love, whose lordly hand Has bridled my desires, And raised my hunger and my thirst To dignity and pride, Let not the strong in me and the constant Eat the bread or drink the wine That tempt my weaker self. Let me rather starve, And let my heart parch with thirst, And let me die and perish, Ere I stretch my hand To a cup you did not fill, Or a bowl you did not bless.
plain: A prayer to love, which has given my desires dignity: let my stronger self not take what tempts my weaker self. I would rather starve and die than reach for a cup love did not fill or bless.
core_idea: Take only what love has blessed

display: The Forerunner: The King-Hermit, paragraph 9
text: Many are those who have given their kingdom for less than solitude and the sweet fellowship of aloneness. Countless are the eagles who descend from the upper air to live with moles that they may know the secrets of the earth. There are those who renounce the kingdom of dreams that they may not seem distant from the dreamless. And those who renounce the kingdom of nakedness and cover their souls that others may not be ashamed in beholding truth uncovered and beauty unveiled.
note: Choosing solitude; hiding truths so others feel comfortable

tags.when_helps: For someone who has chosen solitude, or has stepped down to stay close to others.

display_text: Many are those who have given their kingdom for less than solitude and the sweet fellowship of aloneness. Countless are the eagles who descend from the upper air to live with moles that they may know the secrets of the earth. There are those who renounce the kingdom of dreams that they may not seem distant from the dreamless. And those who renounce the kingdom of nakedness and cover their souls that others may not be ashamed in beholding truth uncovered and beauty unveiled.
plain: Many give up a kingdom for solitude, and eagles come down among moles to learn the earth's secrets. Some give up dreams to stay near the dreamless, or cover their souls so others aren't shamed by naked truth.
core_idea: People give up great things to stay close to others

display: The Forerunner: The Plutocrat, paragraph 1
text: In my wanderings I once saw upon an island a man-headed, iron-hoofed monster who ate of the earth and drank of the sea incessantly. And for a long while I watched him. Then I approached him and said, “Have you never enough; is your hunger never satisfied and your thirst never quenched?” And he answered saying, “Yes, I am satisfied, nay, I am weary of eating and drinking; but I am afraid that tomorrow there will be no more earth to eat and no more sea to drink.”
note: Greed driven by fear of future scarcity

tags.when_helps: For someone who keeps acquiring out of fear of future lack, even when satisfied.

display_text: In my wanderings I once saw upon an island a man-headed, iron-hoofed monster who ate of the earth and drank of the sea incessantly. And for a long while I watched him. Then I approached him and said, “Have you never enough; is your hunger never satisfied and your thirst never quenched?” And he answered saying, “Yes, I am satisfied, nay, I am weary of eating and drinking; but I am afraid that tomorrow there will be no more earth to eat and no more sea to drink.”
plain: On an island I saw a monster endlessly eating earth and drinking sea. I asked if he was never satisfied. He said he was full, even weary of it, but afraid there would be nothing left tomorrow.
core_idea: Fear of tomorrow drives endless craving

display: The Forerunner: War and the Small Nations, paragraph 1
text: Once, high above a pasture, where a sheep and a lamb were grazing, an eagle was circling and gazing hungrily down upon the lamb. And as he was about to descend and seize his prey, another eagle appeared and hovered above the sheep and her young with the same hungry intent. Then the two rivals began to fight filling the sky with their fierce cries. The sheep looked up and was much astonished. She turned to the lamb and said, “How strange, my child, that these two noble birds should attack one another. Is not the vast sky large enough for both of them? Pray, my little one, pray in your heart that God may make peace between your winged brothers.” And the lamb prayed in his heart.
note: Innocent onlookers praying for peace between rivals

tags.when_helps: For someone watching powerful people fight over them, wondering how to respond.

plain: Two eagles circling over a lamb began fighting each other. The astonished sheep told her lamb the sky was large enough for both, and to pray that God make peace between his winged brothers. The lamb prayed.
core_idea: The innocent pray even for their predators

display: The Forerunner: Critics, paragraph 9
text: Then the traveller was much astonished. At last he cried, “My friends, because my horse is stolen, you have hastened one and all to tell me my faults and my shortcomings. But strange, not one word of reproach have you uttered about the man who stole my horse.”
note: Being blamed for misfortune instead of the wrongdoer

tags.when_helps: For someone wronged who finds others blaming them rather than the wrongdoer.

display_text: Then the traveller was much astonished. At last he cried, “My friends, because my horse is stolen, you have hastened one and all to tell me my faults and my shortcomings. But strange, not one word of reproach have you uttered about the man who stole my horse.”
plain: The astonished traveller cried that since his horse was stolen, everyone had rushed to list his faults, yet no one said a word against the thief.
core_idea: People blame the victim, not the wrongdoer

display: The Forerunner: The Weather-Cock, paragraph 1
text: Said the weather-cock to the wind, “How tedious and monotonous you are! Can you not blow any other way but in my face? You disturb my God-given stability.” And the wind did not answer. It only laughed in space.
note: Resenting forces we cannot change

tags.when_helps: For someone irritated that life will not bend to their wishes.

display_text: Said the weather-cock to the wind, “How tedious and monotonous you are! Can you not blow any other way but in my face? You disturb my God-given stability.” And the wind did not answer. It only laughed in space.
plain: The weather-cock complained to the wind that it was dull and always blew in its face, disturbing the stability God gave it. The wind did not answer; it only laughed in space.
core_idea: The vain blame the world for their own position

display: The Forerunner: Out of My Deeper Heart, paragraph 1
text: Out of my deeper heart a bird rose and flew skyward. Higher and higher did it rise, yet larger and larger did it grow. At first it was but like a swallow, then a lark, then an eagle, then as vast as a spring cloud, and then it filled the starry heavens. Out of my heart a bird flew skyward. And it waxed larger as it flew. Yet it left not my heart.
note: Faith that grows yet never leaves the heart

tags.when_helps: For someone whose heart feels expansive and wants to sense how far it reaches.

display_text: Out of my deeper heart a bird rose and flew skyward. Higher and higher did it rise, yet larger and larger did it grow. At first it was but like a swallow, then a lark, then an eagle, then as vast as a spring cloud, and then it filled the starry heavens. Out of my heart a bird flew skyward. And it waxed larger as it flew. Yet it left not my heart.
plain: A bird rose from deep in my heart and flew upward, growing as it rose, from a swallow to something that filled the heavens. Yet it never left my heart.
core_idea: What rises from the heart still stays within it

display: The Forerunner: Out of My Deeper Heart, paragraph 5
text: O my faith, my untamed knowledge, how shall I fly to your height and see with you man’s larger self pencilled upon the sky? How shall I turn this sea within me into mist, and move with you in space immeasurable? How can a prisoner within the temple behold its golden domes? How shall the heart of a fruit be stretched to envelop the fruit also? O my faith, I am in chains behind these bars of silver and ebony, and I cannot fly with you. Yet out of my heart you rise skyward, and it is my heart that holds you, and I shall be content.
note: Longing to rise higher; contentment within limits

tags.when_helps: For someone whose faith outruns their limits, who can be content to hold it in their heart.

display_text: O my faith, my untamed knowledge, how shall I fly to your height and see with you man’s larger self pencilled upon the sky? How shall I turn this sea within me into mist, and move with you in space immeasurable? How can a prisoner within the temple behold its golden domes? How shall the heart of a fruit be stretched to envelop the fruit also? O my faith, I am in chains behind these bars of silver and ebony, and I cannot fly with you. plain: My faith, how can I rise to your height? I am chained like a prisoner who cannot see the temple's domes, and cannot fly with you. Yet you rise from my heart, my heart holds you, and I am content.
core_idea: Faith soars beyond me, yet lives in my heart

plain_judge.issue: Drops the sea-to-mist and fruit-heart images of the self's limits.

display: The Forerunner: “Said a Sheet of Snow-White Paper....”, paragraph 1
text: Said a sheet of snow-white paper, “Pure was I created, and pure will I remain for ever. I would rather be burnt and turn to white ashes than suffer darkness to touch me or the unclean to come near me.” The ink-bottle heard what the paper was saying, and it laughed in its dark heart; but it never dared to approach her. And the multicoloured pencils heard her also, and they too never came near her. And the snow-white sheet of paper did remain pure and chaste for ever--pure and chaste--and empty.
note: Fear of being touched by life leaves you empty

tags.when_helps: For someone keeping themselves so guarded and pure that their life stays empty.

display_text: Said a sheet of snow-white paper, “Pure was I created, and pure will I remain for ever. I would rather be burnt and turn to white ashes than suffer darkness to touch me or the unclean to come near me.” The ink-bottle heard what the paper was saying, and it laughed in its dark heart; but it never dared to approach her. And the multicoloured pencils heard her also, and they too never came near her. And the snow-white sheet of paper did remain pure and chaste for ever--pure and chaste--and empty.
plain: A white sheet of paper vowed to stay pure forever and never let ink or dark touch it. The ink and the coloured pencils kept away. The paper did stay pure and chaste forever, and empty.
core_idea: Purity kept at all costs can leave life empty

display: The Forerunner: Values, paragraph 1
text: Once a man unearthed in his field a marble statue of great beauty. And he took it to a collector who loved all beautiful things and offered it to him for sale, and the collector bought it for a large price. And they parted. And as the man walked home with his money he thought, and he said to himself, “How much life this money means! How can any one give all this for a dead carved stone buried and undreamed of in the earth for a thousand years?” And now the collector was looking at his statue, and he was thinking, and he said to himself, “What beauty! What life! The dream of what a soul!--and fresh with the sweet sleep of a thousand years. How can any one give all this for money, dead and dreamless?”
note: What we value: money versus beauty

tags.when_helps: For someone weighing money against beauty, reminded that value depends on the eye.

plain: A man sold a beautiful statue he had dug up to a collector. Walking home, he wondered how anyone could pay so much for dead stone. The collector wondered how anyone could trade such life for dead money.
core_idea: Each values what the other thinks is dead

display: The Forerunner: Other Seas, paragraph 1
text: A fish said to another fish, “Above this sea of ours there is another sea, with creatures swimming in it--and they live there even as we live here.” The fish replied, “Pure fancy! Pure fancy! When you know that everything that leaves our sea by even an inch, and stays out of it, dies. What proof have you of other lives in other seas?”
note: Doubting other lives or worlds beyond our own

tags.when_helps: For someone sceptical of anything beyond the known, or wondering about life beyond death.

display_text: A fish said to another fish, “Above this sea of ours there is another sea, with creatures swimming in it--and they live there even as we live here.” The fish replied, “Pure fancy! Pure fancy! When you know that everything that leaves our sea by even an inch, and stays out of it, dies. What proof have you of other lives in other seas?”
plain: One fish told another there is a sea above theirs where creatures live as they do. The other scoffed: anything that leaves our sea dies, so what proof is there of life in other seas?
core_idea: We doubt any life beyond what we know

display: The Forerunner: Repentance, paragraph 1
text: On a moonless night a man entered into his neighbour’s garden and stole the largest melon he could find and brought it home. He opened it and found it still unripe. Then behold a marvel! The man’s conscience woke and smote him with remorse; and he repented having stolen the melon.
note: Remorse that arrives for the wrong reason

tags.when_helps: For someone whose conscience stirs late about a wrong, perhaps for the wrong reason.

display_text: On a moonless night a man entered into his neighbour’s garden and stole the largest melon he could find and brought it home. He opened it and found it still unripe. Then behold a marvel! The man’s conscience woke and smote him with remorse; and he repented having stolen the melon.
plain: On a dark night a man stole his neighbour's biggest melon. When he opened it at home and found it unripe, his conscience suddenly woke, and he regretted the theft.
core_idea: Conscience often wakes only when the gain fails

display: The Forerunner: The Dying Man and the Vulture, paragraph 1
text: And the will to die, Stronger than all things strong, Is stayed by a will to live Feebler than all things feeble.
note: The fragile will to live at the end

tags.when_helps: For someone whose will to live feels faint, reminded that even a feeble will can hold.

display_text: And the will to die, Stronger than all things strong, Is stayed by a will to live Feebler than all things feeble.
plain: The wish to die, though stronger than anything, is held back by a wish to live that is weaker than anything.
core_idea: A faint will to live can hold back despair

display: The Forerunner: The Dying Man and the Vulture, paragraph 1
text: It is memory that holds my spirit; A procession of distant days, A vision of youth spent in a dream, A face that bids my eyelids not to sleep, A voice that lingers in my ears, A hand that touches my hand.
note: Memories of loved ones holding us to life

tags.when_helps: For someone haunted by memories of a person or time now gone.

display_text: It is memory that holds my spirit; A procession of distant days, A vision of youth spent in a dream, A face that bids my eyelids not to sleep, A voice that lingers in my ears, A hand that touches my hand.
plain: Memory holds my spirit here: a line of distant days, a youth spent dreaming, a face, a voice that lingers, a hand touching mine.
core_idea: Memories of love hold the spirit back

plain_judge.issue: Flattens "a face that bids my eyelids not to sleep" to "a face".

display: The Forerunner: Beyond My Solitude, paragraph 1
text: Beyond my solitude is another solitude, and to him who dwells therein my aloneness is a crowded market-place and my silence a confusion of sounds. Too young am I and too restless to seek that above-solitude. The voices of yonder valley still hold my ears, and its shadows bar my way and I cannot go.
note: Restlessness; not yet ready for deeper solitude

tags.when_helps: For someone drawn toward deeper solitude yet still held by the world's voices.

display_text: Beyond my solitude is another solitude, and to him who dwells therein my aloneness is a crowded market-place and my silence a confusion of sounds. Too young am I and too restless to seek that above-solitude. The voices of yonder valley still hold my ears, and its shadows bar my way and I cannot go.
plain: Beyond my solitude is a deeper one, to whose dweller my aloneness seems a crowded market and my silence noise. I am too young and restless to seek it; the world's voices and shadows still hold me back.
core_idea: There is always a deeper solitude beyond yours

plain_judge.issue: "The world's voices" interprets "yonder valley" rather than rendering it.

display: The Forerunner: Beyond My Solitude, paragraph 5
text: Beyond this burdened self lives my freer self; and to him my dreams are a battle fought in twilight and my desires the rattling of bones. Too young am I and too outraged to be my freer self. And how shall I become my freer self unless I slay my burdened selves, or unless all men become free? How shall my leaves fly singing upon the wind unless my roots shall wither in the dark? How shall the eagle in me soar against the sun until my fledglings leave the nest which I with my own beak have built for them?
note: Longing for a freer self; letting go to grow

tags.when_helps: For someone who longs for a freer self but feels bound by burdens and responsibilities.

display_text: Beyond this burdened self lives my freer self; and to him my dreams are a battle fought in twilight and my desires the rattling of bones. How shall my leaves fly singing upon the wind unless my roots shall wither in the dark? plain: Beyond my burdened self lives a freer self, but I am too young and angry to be it. How can I be free unless my burdened selves die, or all people are free, or my roots wither and fledglings leave?
core_idea: Freedom requires letting go of what holds you

plain_judge.issue: Compresses roots, leaves and eagle images into a list; drops their logic.

display: The Forerunner: The Last Watch, paragraph 14
text: You would drink love from a cup, but not from a surging river. You would hear love’s faint murmur, but when love shouts you would muffle your ears.
note: Love rejected for being too abundant

tags.when_helps: For someone who wants love but shrinks from its full force.

display_text: You would drink love from a cup, but not from a surging river. You would hear love’s faint murmur, but when love shouts you would muffle your ears.
plain: You want love in a cup, not as a rushing river. You listen to its faint murmur, but when love shouts you cover your ears.
core_idea: We want love only in small, safe amounts

display: The Forerunner: The Last Watch, paragraph 33
text: Night is over, and we children of night must die when dawn comes leaping upon the hills; and out of our ashes a mightier love shall rise. And it shall laugh in the sun, and it shall be deathless.
note: Renewal: a mightier love rising from ashes

tags.when_helps: For someone at the end of a dark chapter, needing hope that a greater love will rise.

display_text: Night is over, and we children of night must die when dawn comes leaping upon the hills; and out of our ashes a mightier love shall rise. And it shall laugh in the sun, and it shall be deathless.
plain: Night is ending, and we children of night must die at dawn; from our ashes a stronger love will rise, laughing in the sun and never dying.
core_idea: From our ending a deathless love will rise
